source_excerpt:
A little cyberpunk companion for your Windows desktop.
Capri is a lightweight desktop pet inspired by the atmosphere of Cyberpunk 2077 . She lives on your desktop as an animated character, with a compact terminal-style chat window powered by a local Ollama model.
The goal is to make Capri feel like a companion you can hang out with while you work---not another giant assistant dashboard.
Desktop pet: an animated character that stays on the desktop.
Idle behaviour: animation states such as blinking and sleeping/waking.
Terminal-style chat: a compact cyberpunk-inspired chat window.
Local AI: replies are generated by Ollama using the custom capri:latest model.
Streaming responses: text appears as the model generates it.
Custom personality: Capri's persona is configured in the Ollama Modelfile , rather than duplicated in the Python UI code.
Local-first text chat: the current text-chat flow is designed to run without a hosted AI API.
In progress: voice input and spoken replies are planned. Push-to-talk speech recognition and local text-to-speech are not implemented yet.
Gemma 3 4B --- base model for the custom capri:latest model
faster-whisper + Piper --- planned options for local speech-to-text and text-to-speech

The chat UI should insert streamed model chunks as plain text, not HTML. In the streaming-token handler, use QTextCursor.insertText() or QTextEdit.insertPlainText() so whitespace is preserved.
The current text-generation flow is designed to use a local Ollama model. Voice features are still planned; before enabling them, verify that microphone audio, transcripts, and generated speech stay local and aren't sent to external services.
Issues, bug reports, and improvements are welcome. Keep changes small and test the desktop UI and model connection after modifying the chat or character code.
Capri is an open-source, Cyberpunk-inspired desktop companion that lives on your Windows desktop. Built with local AI using Ollama, she can hang out and chat with you. Voice interaction and more animations are planned. Contributions, ideas, and feedback are welcome!
